source.original_text: Let n>=3 and kappa>=4. For O in the full real orthogonal group, let A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T) be the existing literal precision, and define the explicit real formula p_O(x)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A_O x/2) on real coordinate n-space, with n/2 a real exponent. For every vector x, O -> det(O)p_O(x) is absolutely integrable under the actual canonical normalized full-O(n) Haar probability. For every fixed Q in full O(n), including reflections, E[det(O)p_O(Qx)]=E[det(O)p_O(x)]. This statement concerns the displayed formula itself and does not identify it with the density of an actual Gaussian probability law.

decoder_context: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R is the full real orthogonal group, with inherited real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. Both determinant signs are allowed.

Measure.haarMeasure on top is the actual normalized probability measure on the whole compact group; probability/compactness are supplied internally. It is not an arbitrary or special-orthogonal measure.

Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root. Powers with exponent (n:R)/2 are real powers; the dimension is not truncated by natural-number division. Integrable means actual absolute Bochner L1 under the displayed full Haar law.

/-!
# Rotation invariance of the literal signed Gaussian kernel average

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.2 p4.1, the fixed-Q
conjugation step underlying Ex58. The displayed kernel is literal; its
identification as the density of an actual Gaussian law is a separate obligation.
Orthogonal transitivity, the norm-axis identity, spatial Fubini and TV are separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelRotation

private lemma haar_conjugation {n : ℕ} (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => Q * O * Q⁻¹) = orthogonalHaar n := by
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).2.1
  have hr : (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => O * Q⁻¹) = orthogonalHaar n := by
    apply (orthogonalHaar_spec n).2.2
    · exact Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map (by fun_prop)
    · infer_instance
  have heq : (fun O => Q * O * Q⁻¹) =
      (fun O => Q * O) ∘ (fun O => O * Q⁻¹) := by
    funext O
    exact mul_assoc Q O Q⁻¹
  rw [heq, ← Measure.map_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop), hr,
    orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left]

private lemma conjugation_algebra {n : ℕ} (κ : ℝ)
    (Q O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    singleBlockPrecision κ (Q * O * Q⁻¹) =
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * singleBlockPrecision κ O *
          (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose ∧
    ((Q * O * Q⁻¹ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det =
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det ∧
    (singleBlockPrecision κ (Q * O * Q⁻¹)).det = (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det ∧
    ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ,
      ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x) ⬝ᵥ
        (singleBlockPrecision κ (Q * O * Q⁻¹) *ᵥ
          ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x)) =
      x ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ x) := by
  have hQ : (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose = 1 :=
    (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff (Fin n) ℝ).mp Q.property
  have hQt : (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) = 1 :=
    (Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff' (Fin n) ℝ).mp Q.property
  have hinv : ((Q⁻¹ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) =
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose := by ext i j; rfl
  have hcoe : ((Q * O * Q⁻¹ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
      Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) =
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose := by
    simp only [Matrix.UnitaryGroup.mul_val, hinv]
  have hA : singleBlockPrecision κ (Q * O * Q⁻¹) =
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * singleBlockPrecision κ O *
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose := by
    simp only [singleBlockPrecision, hcoe, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_transpose,
      Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, Matrix.smul_mul,
      Matrix.mul_add, Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_assoc, hQ]
  have hd : (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1 := by
    simpa only [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose, Matrix.det_one] using congrArg Matrix.det hQ
  have hdet (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
      ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * M *
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose).det = M.det := by
    simp only [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose]
    calc
      _ = M.det * ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det) := by ring
      _ = M.det := by rw [hd, mul_one]
  refine ⟨hA, by rw [hcoe, hdet], by rw [hA, hdet], ?_⟩
  intro x
  rw [hA]
  have hm : ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * singleBlockPrecision κ O *
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose) *ᵥ
        ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x) =
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ x) := by
    simp only [Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, Matrix.mul_assoc, hQt, Matrix.mul_one]
  rw [hm, dotProduct_comm, ← Matrix.dotProduct_transpose_mulVec,
    Matrix.mulVec_mulVec, hQt, Matrix.one_mulVec, dotProduct_comm]

theorem signed_kernel_rotation_invariant {n : ℕ} (_hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (_hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ :=
      fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
        (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-(x ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ x)) / 2)
    (∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x) (orthogonalHaar n)) ∧
    ∀ (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : Fin n → ℝ),
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          p O ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x) ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
  classical
  let p : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ :=
    fun O x => Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) *
        Real.exp (-(x ⬝ᵥ (singleBlockPrecision κ O *ᵥ x)) / 2)
  change (∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x) (orthogonalHaar n)) ∧ _
  have hAc : Continuous (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => singleBlockPrecision κ O) := by
    unfold singleBlockPrecision
    exact continuous_const.sub
      ((continuous_subtype_val.add continuous_subtype_val.matrix_transpose).const_smul ((κ - 1) / 4))
  have hcont (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Continuous (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x) := by
    dsimp only [p]
    fun_prop
  have hL1 (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x) (orthogonalHaar n) := by
    let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
    exact (hcont x).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport (isClosed_tsupport _).isCompact
  refine ⟨hL1, ?_⟩
  intro Q x
  have hcov (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
      ((Q * O * Q⁻¹ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
        p (Q * O * Q⁻¹) ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x) =
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * p O x := by
    obtain ⟨_, hd, hA, hquad⟩ := conjugation_algebra κ Q O
    dsimp only [p]
    rw [hd, hA, hquad]
  have hemb : MeasurableEmbedding (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Q * O * Q⁻¹) :=
    ((Homeomorph.mulLeft Q).trans (Homeomorph.mulRight Q⁻¹)).measurableEmbedding
  calc
    _ = ∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        ((Q * O * Q⁻¹ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          p (Q * O * Q⁻¹) ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x) ∂orthogonalHaar n := by
      have hmp : MeasurePreserving
          (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Q * O * Q⁻¹)
          (orthogonalHaar n) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
        ⟨hemb.measurable, haar_conjugation Q⟩
      exact (hmp.integral_comp hemb (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          p O ((Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ x))).symm
    _ = _ := by apply integral_congr_ae; exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall hcov

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.KernelRotation

lesson.statement: Let n>=3 and kappa>=4. For O in the full real orthogonal group, let A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T) be the existing literal precision, and define the explicit real formula p_O(x)=sqrt(det A_O)/(2pi)^(n/2) exp(-x^T A_O x/2) on real coordinate n-space, with n/2 a real exponent. For every vector x, O -> det(O)p_O(x) is absolutely integrable under the actual canonical normalized full-O(n) Haar probability. For every fixed Q in full O(n), including reflections, E[det(O)p_O(Qx)]=E[det(O)p_O(x)]. This statement concerns the displayed formula itself and does not identify it with the density of an actual Gaussian probability law.
assumptions: The AppendixB2 standing bounds n>=3 and kappa>=4 are retained, although the explicit algebraic invariance proof needs less. No L1, continuity or covariance hypothesis is added.
The law is the same actual canonical normalized Borel Haar probability on the full real O(n); both determinant components are allowed.
Vectors are real coordinates on Fin n, dotProduct is the Euclidean quadratic form and Q acts by matrix multiplication. The formula uses real exponent (n:R)/2 and the nonnegative real square root.
The local formula p is literal. This theorem defines no Gaussian probability measure and assumes no density identification, normalization or covariance fact. Those remain separate obligations.

steps.title: Conjugate the actual precision
steps.text: Let C_Q(O)=QOQ^T. Expanding the existing literal precision, transpose reverses products and QQ^T=I. Thus conjugating O conjugates A_O by the same Q. This calculation is internal, not an extra covariance premise.
steps.lean: Private conjugation_algebra proves hA by the exact source precision body, transpose/matrix distributivity and both orthogonality identities.

steps.title: Preserve both determinant factors
steps.text: Taking determinants in QQ^T=I gives (det Q)^2=1. Therefore conjugation preserves det(O), as a signed real number, and det(A_O). The square-root normalization in the literal kernel is consequently unchanged. No det Q=+1 restriction is imposed.
steps.lean: The same private provider derives hd and hdet from Matrix.det_mul and Matrix.det_transpose, then obtains the exact determinant equalities.

steps.title: Transport the quadratic exponent
steps.text: The conjugated precision and Q^T Q=I imply (Qx)^T A_{C_Q(O)}(Qx)=x^T A_Ox. Combining this with determinant preservation yields pointwise covariance for the literal kernel and its determinant weight.
steps.lean: conjugation_algebra proves the quadratic identity by actual mulVec and dotProduct transpose identities. The public proof combines it with the determinant facts in hcov.

steps.title: Keep exactly the same full Haar law
steps.text: The right translate of the actual Haar probability is still a Haar probability, so its uniqueness characterization identifies it with the original law. Compose that right translation with the existing canonical fixed-left invariance theorem. Their composition is C_Q, hence conjugation preserves the actual normalized full Haar law.
steps.lean: Private haar_conjugation consumes orthogonalHaar_spec, the canonical Mathlib Haar right-translation instance and Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map, then genuinely calls orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left. No arbitrary invariant law or assumed conjugation identity is supplied.

steps.title: Prove every fixed-vector average finite
steps.text: For fixed x, the precision entries, determinant and square root are continuous functions of O. The finite quadratic form and exponential preserve continuity. On compact O(n), this determinant-weighted formula has compact support and is integrable under the actual finite Haar probability. This proves the L1 output, including x=0.
steps.lean: hAc and hcont establish actual continuity; hL1 uses orthogonalHaar_spec and Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport. This is fixed-x Haar L1 only, not joint spatial domination or Fubini.

steps.title: Change variables inside the genuine Haar average
steps.text: Apply the measure-preserving conjugation substitution to the integrand O -> det(O)p_O(Qx), then use the pointwise covariance. The same normalized law appears on both sides and no exchange of spatial integrals occurs.
steps.lean: The public proof builds the actual conjugation measurable embedding and MeasurePreserving map, applies MeasurePreserving.integral_comp, and finishes by integral_congr_ae with hcov. Orthogonal transitivity to the norm-axis point is not asserted here.

lesson.lean_statement: The local let spells out the complete real Gaussian formula; absolute integrability and every fixed-Q identity are conclusions.
lesson.lean_proof: Two reachable private providers produce actual Haar conjugation preservation and all precision/determinant/quadratic covariance facts; the public proof proves L1 and consumes both providers in the final average identity.

candidate_assumptions.source: AppendixB2 standing n>=3,kappa>=4; full Haar O(n), every Q and x. p4.1 uses the Gaussian density p_O and its conjugation covariance.
candidate_assumptions.lean: Same standing range and full Haar; the real formula p_O is explicit. Fixed-x Haar L1 and covariance/measure preservation are internal outputs. Identification with a Gaussian probability density remains a separate excluded source obligation.

reconstruction.text: For every natural number n satisfying n >= 3 and every real number kappa satisfying kappa >= 4, let G = O(n) = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R be the full real orthogonal group, including both determinant signs, and let mu = Measure.haarMeasure (top : PositiveCompacts G) be normalized Haar probability on the whole group, with the inherited real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. Let V = (Fin n -> R); vectors are finite real coordinate functions. For O in G, identify O with its underlying real n by n matrix and set A(O) = ((kappa + 1)/2) I_n - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T). Define the literal real function p : G -> V -> R by p(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2*pi)^((n:R)/2) * exp(-(x dot (A(O)x))/2). Here sqrt is the nonnegative real square root, the displayed power is a real power with real division after coercion of n to R, dot is the finite Euclidean dot product, and matrix action is matrix-vector multiplication. Then the conjunction of these assertions holds: (1) for every x in V, the function O |-> det(O) * p(O,x) is Bochner integrable in the actual absolute L1 sense under mu; (2) for every Q in G and every x in V, integral over G of det(O) * p(O,Qx) dmu(O) equals integral over G of det(O) * p(O,x) dmu(O). In the second assertion Qx is the action of the underlying matrix Q by matrix-vector multiplication. The function p is specified pointwise as a real-valued formula; it is not a newly constructed probability law and no premise identifying a density is imposed.
